items.title: Sound and Wind Are Not Always There

items.zh: 復次，聲於一切色聚中，界故說有，相即不定。由現在方便生故。
items.en: Further, as for sound: in every matter aggregate, it is present in the sense of its causal element, but its actual mark is not fixed. This is because sound arises only given a present, contributing condition.

items.zh: 風有二種。謂恒相續及不恒相續。恒相續者，謂於彼彼聚有恒旋轉風。不恒相續者，謂旋風及空行風。
items.en: Wind is of two kinds: continuous and non-continuous. The continuous kind refers to the constantly circulating wind present within this or that aggregate. The non-continuous kind refers to whirlwinds and winds that move through open space.

items.title: Darkness and Light Are Kinds of Matter Too

items.zh: 又闇色、明色，說名空界及孔隙。
items.en: Further, darkness and light are called the sphere of open space, and the sphere of an opening or cavity.

items.zh: 又諸闇色恒相續者，謂世界中間；不恒相續者，謂於餘處。
items.en: As for darkness that continues without interruption: this refers to the interval between world-systems. As for darkness that does not continue without interruption: this refers to every other place.

items.zh: 如是明色恒相續者，謂於自然光明天中；不恒相續者，謂於餘處。
items.en: Light that continues without interruption, in the same way, refers to the naturally luminous heavens. Light that does not continue without interruption refers to every other place.

items.zh: 又明闇色，謂於顯色增聚應知。
items.en: Further, it should be understood that light and darkness are simply an intensification within the category of visible colour.

items.zh: 又由依止色聚種子功能故，若遇相似緣時，或小聚無間大聚生，或大聚無間小聚生。由此因緣，施設諸聚有增有減。
items.en: Further, owing to the function inherent in the seed of a matter aggregate, when a similar condition is met, a small aggregate may immediately give rise to a large aggregate, or a large aggregate may immediately give rise to a small one. For this reason, matter aggregates are said to increase and decrease.

items.zh: 如經言：若堅、堅攝、近攝、非近攝、執受，乃至廣說。堅云何？謂地。堅攝云何？謂彼種子。
items.en: As the sutra says: solidity, what belongs to solidity, what is held near, what is not held near, what is grasped by consciousness — and so on, at length. What is solidity? It is the earth element. What belongs to solidity? It is the seed of that same element.

items.zh: 又堅者，即彼界。堅攝者，謂髮毛等，或土塊等。
items.en: Further, solidity is that very causal element itself; what belongs to solidity is hair, body-hair, and the like, or a clod of earth, and the like.

items.zh: 近攝云何？謂有執受。執受云何？謂內所攝。非近攝云何？謂無執受。無執受云何？謂外所攝。
items.en: What is held near? It is what is grasped by consciousness. What is grasped by consciousness? It is what is comprised within the internal body. What is not held near? It is what is not grasped by consciousness. What is not grasped by consciousness? It is what is comprised in the external world.

items.zh: 又心心所所執種子，名近攝，名執受；與此相違，名非近攝，名非執受。又隨逐自身故，名近攝、執受，如前說。
items.en: Further, a seed that is grasped by mind and mental factors is called held near, and is called grasped by consciousness; the opposite of this is called not held near, and not grasped by consciousness. Further, because it follows along with one's own body, it is called held near and grasped by consciousness, as explained above.

items.zh: 如是水等界，如理應知。
items.en: The water element, and the rest, should be understood in just the same way.

items.title: All Four Elements Are Present in Everything, Always

items.zh: 又於一切色聚中，一切時具有一切大種界。如世間現見乾薪等物，鑽即火生，擊石等亦爾。
items.en: Further, within every matter aggregate, at all times, every one of the four great elements is present as a causal element. As is commonly observed in the world: dry firewood, when drilled, produces fire; striking flint against stone likewise produces fire.

items.zh: 又銅鐵金銀等、極火所燒即銷為水。從月愛珠，水便流出。
items.en: Further, copper, iron, gold, silver, and the like, when melted by intense fire, turn to a liquid state; and from the moon-loving pearl, water flows forth.

items.zh: 又得神通者，由心勝解力，變大地等成金銀等。
items.en: Further, one who has attained supernormal power can, through the force of the mind's resolute conviction, transform the great earth and the like into gold, silver, and so on.

items.zh: 又色聚有三種流轉。一者、長養，二者、等流，三者、異熟生。
items.en: Further, a matter aggregate continues in existence through three processes: first, nourishment; second, homogeneous outflow; third, karmic-ripening arising.

items.zh: 長養有二種。一、處遍滿長養，二、相增盛長養。
items.en: Nourishment is of two kinds: first, nourishment that fills out its extent; second, nourishment that intensifies its characteristic.

items.zh: 等流有四種。一、長養等流，二、異熟等流，三、變異等流，四、自性等流。
items.en: Homogeneous outflow is of four kinds: first, the homogeneous outflow of nourishment; second, the homogeneous outflow of karmic ripening; third, the homogeneous outflow of transformation; fourth, the homogeneous outflow of its own nature.

items.zh: 異熟生有二種。一、異熟體生，名異熟生；二、從異熟生，名異熟生。
items.en: Karmic-ripening arising is of two kinds: first, that which arises as the very substance of ripening, called karmic-ripening arising; second, that which arises from ripening, likewise called karmic-ripening arising.

items.zh: 又諸色聚，略說依六處轉。謂建立處、覆藏處、資具處、根所依處、根處、三摩地所行處。
items.en: Further, matter aggregates, briefly stated, occur dependent on six places: the place of foundation, the place of shelter, the place of provisions, the place a sense-faculty depends on, the place of the sense-faculty itself, and the place where meditative absorption operates.

items.title: The Mind and Its Fifty-Three Companions

items.zh: 復次，於心心所品中，有心可得，及五十三心所可得。謂作意等，乃至尋伺為後邊，如前說。
items.en: Further, within the category of mind and mental factors, there is mind itself, and fifty-three mental factors, to be found — namely, attention and the rest, down to investigation and analysis at the furthest end, as already explained.

items.title: Five Questions About When a Mental Factor Arises

items.zh: 問：如是諸心所，幾依一切處心生，一切地、一切時、一切耶？答：五。謂作意等，思為後邊。
items.en: Question: Of these mental factors, how many arise together with mind in every moral quality, every ground, every time, and every instance of mind? Answer: Five — attention, and the rest, down to volition at the furthest end.

items.zh: 幾依一切處心生，一切地，非一切時、非一切耶？答：亦五。謂欲等，慧為後邊。
items.en: How many arise together with mind in every moral quality and every ground, but not every time and not every instance of mind? Also five — aspiration, and the rest, down to wisdom at the furthest end.

items.zh: 幾唯依善，非一切處心生；然一切地，非一切時、非一切耶？答：謂信等，不害為後邊。
items.en: How many arise only together with a wholesome mind — not in every moral quality — yet in every ground, though not every time and not every instance of mind? Faith, and the rest, down to non-harming at the furthest end.

items.zh: 幾唯依染污，非一切處心生，非一切地、非一切時、非一切耶？答：謂貪等，不正知為後邊。
items.en: How many arise only together with a defiled mind — not in every moral quality, not in every ground, not every time, and not every instance of mind? Craving, and the rest, down to incorrect awareness at the furthest end.

items.zh: 幾依一切處心生，非一切地、非一切時、非一切耶？答：謂惡作等，伺為後邊。
items.en: How many arise together with mind in every moral quality, but not in every ground, not every time, and not every instance of mind? Regret, and the rest, down to sustained thought at the furthest end.

items.zh: 復次，根不壞境界現前，能生作意正起，爾時從彼識乃得生。

items.title: Two Ways a Sense-Faculty Can Fail

items.zh: 云何根不壞？謂有二種因。一、不滅壞故；二、不羸劣故。
items.en: What is meant by "the sense-faculty is not impaired"? There are two causes: first, that it is not destroyed; second, that it is not weakened.

items.zh: 云何境界現前？謂或由所依處故，或由自性故，或由方故，或由時故，或由顯了不顯了故，或由全分及一分故。
items.en: What is meant by "the object is present"? It is by reason of the base it depends on; or by reason of its own nature; or by reason of direction; or by reason of time; or by reason of whether it is manifest or unmanifest; or by reason of whether the whole, or only a part, is taken.

items.title: Four Obstructions, and Two Kinds of "Too Far"

items.zh: 若四種障所不障礙，亦非極遠。謂覆蔽障、隱沒障、映奪障、幻惑障。
items.en: Provided it is not obstructed by any of four kinds of obstruction, and is not at an extreme distance. Namely: the obstruction of concealment, the obstruction of being hidden away, the obstruction of being overwhelmed, and the obstruction of illusion.

items.zh: 極遠有二種。謂處所極遠、損減極遠。
items.en: Extreme distance is of two kinds: distance of place, and distance through attenuation.

items.zh: 云何能生作意正起？由四因故。一、由欲力，二、由念力，三、由境界力，四、由數習力。
items.en: What gives rise to the arising of attention? It is due to four causes: first, the force of desire; second, the force of mindfulness; third, the force of the object itself; fourth, the force of habituation.

items.zh: 云何由欲力？謂若於是處心有愛著，心則於彼多作意生。云何由念力？謂若於彼已善取其相、已極作想，心則於彼多作意生。
items.en: What is the force of desire? Wherever the mind is attached with fondness, the mind generates attention towards that place, again and again. What is the force of mindfulness? Wherever a mark has already been thoroughly grasped and thoroughly dwelt upon, the mind generates attention towards that place, again and again.

items.zh: 云何由境界力？謂若彼境界或極廣大、或極可意正現在前，心則於彼多作意生。云何由數習力？若於彼境界已極串習、已極諳悉，心即於彼多作意生。
items.en: What is the force of the object? Whenever an object is either extremely vast, or extremely pleasing, and is directly present, the mind generates attention towards it, again and again. What is the force of habituation? Wherever an object has already been thoroughly practised and thoroughly mastered, the mind generates attention towards it, again and again.

items.zh: 若異此者，應於一所緣境，唯一作意一切時生。
items.en: Were it otherwise, attention towards a single object would arise in only a single, fixed way, at every single time.

blocks.text: Today's reading finishes the account of matter and turns to mind. The first part answers a series of small questions about matter: is sound always present? are darkness and light matter? what makes matter "mine"? The second part sorts the fifty-three mental factors by four tests, and the third returns to a topic from Day 2: what exactly must be present for a consciousness to arise.

One sentence is untranslated (0291a12–a13): "Further, when the faculty is unimpaired and the object present, and the attention that produces it properly arises, then consciousness arises from that." It restates Day 2's three conditions before the treatise explains each.

subs.head: Sound and wind; darkness and light

blocks.text: Sound is present in every aggregate "in the sense of its causal element, but its actual mark is not fixed": every piece of matter can sound, but actual sound needs a present condition. Venerable Miào Jìng: "element" here means "cause". Wind likewise may be constant or occasional.

Darkness and light are kinds of visible form. Unbroken darkness is found "in the interval between world-systems"; both teachers read this, following the *Lotus Sūtra*, as the gap between one trichiliocosm and the next, where sun and moon never shine (Day 13).

Aggregates increase and decrease. Venerable Miào Jìng's example: in Kāśyapa Buddha's time it took a day and a night to climb Vulture Peak; by Śākyamuni's time one reached the top in moments. The mountain had shrunk, along with beings' merit.

The treatise explains sūtra terms. "Solidity" is the earth element; "what belongs to solidity" is its seed. Matter "held near" (親附) means matter **grasped by consciousness** (執受), the word "appropriate" again. Venerable Miào Jìng's test: cutting hair or nails does not hurt, because that part of the body is not grasped. Only matter the ālayavijñāna holds can feel.

"Within every matter aggregate, at all times, every one of the four great elements is present as a causal element." Proof: dry wood or flint produces fire when struck; metal melts into liquid; water flows from the "moon-loving pearl"; one with supernormal powers can turn earth into gold by resolute conviction. The latent elements need only a condition to appear.

Matter depends on six "places": foundation, shelter, provisions, the place a faculty depends on, the faculty itself, and the sphere where meditation operates. Do not confuse this with the "six supports" of Day 13; the lists are similar.

The category of mind contains mind itself and fifty-three mental factors. The treatise sorts them by four tests: does a factor arise in every moral quality (wholesome, defiled, indeterminate), in every ground, at every time, and with every instance of mind?

items: The five **universal** factors (attention, contact, feeling, perception, volition) pass all four tests.
The five **particular** factors (desire, resolve, mindfulness, concentration, wisdom) occur in every moral quality and every ground, but not at every time or with every mind.
The wholesome factors, beginning with faith, occur only with a wholesome mind, yet in every ground; not at every time or with every mind.
The defiled factors occur only with a defiled mind, and only in some grounds.

blocks.text: The two teachers explain "every ground" differently: Venerable Miào Jìng as the three grounds of this treatise (with investigation and analysis, with analysis only, with neither), Master Cháng Bǎi as the nine grounds of the three realms. Both readings work; they cut the same territory differently.
These four tests are the origin of the familiar six groups of mental factors in the *Hundred Dharmas*.
Day 2 named three conditions; now each is analysed.

items: **The faculty is unimpaired**: neither destroyed (as in blindness) nor weakened (as in poor sight). Venerable Miào Jìng notes that the body-faculty can never be completely destroyed, or the person would not exist.

**The object is present**: not blocked by one of four obstructions: concealment, being hidden away, being overwhelmed, or illusion; nor too far away in place or too subtle. Both teachers' example of being overwhelmed: stars are in the sky by day, but the sun's light eclipses them.

**Attention properly arises**, triggered by one of four forces: desire, mindfulness, the object, or habituation. Venerable Miào Jìng, following Kuījī, maps them onto time: desire looks to the future, mindfulness to the past, the object is present, and habituation spans all three.

blocks.text: Read in reverse, this is a guide to restraint of the senses. We cannot always change the faculty or the object, but attention, which is driven by desire and habit, is where training works.

quiz.q: The text says sound is "present in every matter aggregate in the sense of its causal element, but its actual mark is not fixed." What does this mean?
options: every aggregate is constantly making sound
only living beings have sound
every aggregate carries the cause (element) of sound, but actual sound arises only given a present contributing condition
sound is merely conceptual
quiz.why: "As for sound: in every matter aggregate, it is present in the sense of its causal element, but its actual mark is not fixed. This is because sound arises only given a present, contributing condition." Venerable Miào Jìng: "element" here means "cause"; "as cause, sound is in all the four elements … when it comes to the actual mark of sound, that is not fixed." Master Cháng Bǎi: a struck table, clapped hands, a rung bell — every material thing can sound, but only when the condition is met.

quiz.q: The treatise says "held near" means "grasped by consciousness." According to Venerable Miào Jìng, what does "grasped" mean, and what example does he give?
options: holding something in one's hand
mind lodging in matter — though all is manifested by the ālayavijñāna, cutting hair or nails does not hurt; that part is not grasped
attachment to possessions
keeping precepts
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "'Near' means mind — the ālayavijñāna and the first six consciousnesses … mind lodging in matter is what 'grasped' means." And: "We can cut our hair with scissors … but it doesn't hurt. When nails grow long we trim them, and that doesn't hurt either"; "though all is manifested by the ālayavijñāna, there is a difference between grasped and not grasped." Master Cháng Bǎi: pull a hair at the scalp and it hurts (grasped); once cut, the hair is no longer felt.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT among the "six places" on which matter aggregates depend?
options: the place of foundation
the place a sense-faculty depends on
the place where meditative absorption operates
the place of security
quiz.why: The six are: the place of foundation, of shelter, of provisions, the place a faculty depends on, the faculty itself, and the place where absorption operates. D, "security," belongs to the six supports of fascicle 2, §47 — similar-sounding and easily confused. Venerable Miào Jìng groups the six into three: the first three are matter outside the body, the faculty's base and the faculty belong to the living body, and the last is form in the sphere of dharmas.

quiz.q: Which mental factors arise "in every moral quality, every ground, every time, and every instance of mind" — passing all four tests?
options: the five: attention, contact, feeling, ideation, and volition
the five: aspiration, resolve, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom
the eleven wholesome factors beginning with faith
regret, drowsiness, investigation, and analysis
quiz.why: "How many arise together with mind in every moral quality, every ground, every time, and every instance of mind? Answer: Five — attention, and the rest, down to volition." These are the five universals. B, the five object-determined factors, pass the first two tests but not "every time" or "every instance." Venerable Miào Jìng: the universal factors "get along anywhere, without obstruction."

quiz.q: How do the wholesome factors beginning with faith fare on the four tests?
options: they pass all four
they pass none
every moral quality and every ground, but not every time or every instance
only with a wholesome mind, not every moral quality; yet every ground; not every time, not every instance
quiz.why: "How many arise only together with a wholesome mind — not in every moral quality — yet in every ground, though not every time and not every instance of mind? Faith, and the rest, down to non-harming." C describes the object-determined five. B describes the defiled factors, which fail all four. Venerable Miào Jìng: the wholesome factors are not "every moral quality" because even the desire realm's ground has evil in it, not only good.

quiz.q: What are the four obstructions named in the treatise?
options: the obstructions of affliction, karma, result, and the knowable
greed, hatred, delusion, and conceit
far, near, large, small
concealment, being hidden away, being overwhelmed, and illusion
quiz.why: "The obstruction of concealment, the obstruction of being hidden away, the obstruction of being overwhelmed, and the obstruction of illusion." There are also two kinds of "extreme distance": of place and of attenuation. A lists obstructions spoken of elsewhere; these four are ways a present object fails to be seen. Venerable Miào Jìng: concealment is like darkness or a storehouse — at a deeper level ignorance is a concealment too; being hidden away is by drugs or spells.

quiz.q: The treatise names four forces that trigger attention: desire, mindfulness, the object, and habituation. According to Kuījī as cited by Venerable Miào Jìng, how do they map onto the three times?
options: all four are present
desire is future, mindfulness past, the object present, and habituation spans all three
desire is past, mindfulness future
they have nothing to do with time
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Kuījī explains: the force of desire refers to the future, the force of mindfulness to the past, the force of the object to the present, and the force of habituation spans all three times." The text closes by noting that without these four, "attention towards a single object would arise in only a single, fixed way, at every single time" — which plainly is not how experience works.
